source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA, GAO, DoD, and NIST references on 2026-08-31. Nine URLs returned HTTP 200 directly. GAO-20-48G was retrievable through the official GAO indexed product record, while the official page and report assets rejected the command-line client with HTTP 403; no availability claim beyond verified indexed retrieval is made. Reviewed NASA technology assessment/insertion, GAO technology readiness, active DoD SD-22, NIST CSF 2.0 examples, and NASA decision, risk, configuration, verification, validation, and NPR guidance. Institutional and acquisition-specific scopes are explicit.

evidence: Reviewed context-specific technology record T(o,x) and definitions for capability, maturity, integration, support, security, evidence, transition, and uncertainty.
Reviewed feasible-option set under required capability and noncompensable constraints before lifecycle-value comparison.
Reviewed current, target, and time/effectivity-dependent transition configurations.
Confirmed readiness level is treated as an ordinal contextual summary rather than probability of success or a system-wide scalar.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates technology maturity, integrated product readiness, transition state, operational evidence, and authority.

evidence: Executed technology-refresh-options-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-087/report.json.
Recomputed legacy patch score as 36, modular refresh as 48, and full replacement as 42.
Confirmed modular refresh has the highest declared score with a six-point margin.
Recomputed Exercise 2 scores after increasing transition-feasibility weight to six: legacy 51, modular 60, full replacement 45.
Confirmed all arithmetic uses declared integer weights and ordinal ratings only.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Ordinal weighted sums do not validate scales, weights, independence, completeness, maturity evidence, feasibility, uncertainty, risk, or authorization.

evidence: Confirmed newer technology does not entail greater lifecycle value in a specified system context.
Confirmed commercial or heritage success does not entail readiness in a new architecture, environment, scale, data distribution, or use.
Confirmed technology readiness does not entail integrated product verification, operational validation, producibility, supportability, or transition success.
Confirmed a weighted-score maximum cannot override a noncompensable safety, security, legal, or mission constraint.
Confirmed online deployment does not entail effectivity completion or superseded-stack retirement.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Implication limits prevent maturity ratings, prototypes, rankings, and rollout indicators from becoming false proof.

evidence: Challenged vendor-led scope, heritage transfer, unrepresentative prototypes, happy-path demonstrations, immature development hidden in integration, and unsupported score precision.
Challenged timing/resource/interface semantics, state/data migration, humans, physical integration, suppliers/processes, tools, security/privacy, certification, and recovery dependencies.

Challenged mixed versions, adapters becoming permanent, offline fleets, spares/repairs, disaster recovery, customer variants, dual-stack drift, and premature old-stack removal or indefinite retention.

Challenged rollback after irreversible data/physical/credential/contract changes, managed-service exit, proprietary rights, portfolio common cause, specialist capacity, and simultaneous changes that defeat diagnosis.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limitations, uncertainty, effectivity, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real refresh decisions require applicable system/domain, architecture, technology, software/data/platform, supplier/manufacturing, human factors, operations/support, security/safety/privacy, V&V, finance/contracts, records, and technical-authority expertise.

evidence: Confirmed refresh begins from capability, obligation, current baseline, actual population, service horizon, risk, and decision window.
Confirmed roadmap aligns architecture, maturity, obsolescence, supply, security, workforce, investment, deployment, fallback, and triggers.
Confirmed readiness evidence names exact technology configuration, intended function, representative environment, integration, scale, failure/security conditions, supply, and limitations.
Confirmed alternatives pass mandatory constraints before scoring and retain underlying evidence, uncertainty, sensitivity, fallback, and descope.
Confirmed transition includes configuration/provenance, migration, coexistence, cohorts, V&V, monitoring, anomaly response, recovery, training, communication, and effectivity.
Confirmed closure reconciles actual target state and dispositions old technology, adapters, data, access, inventory, tools, contracts, evidence, and records.
invariant_checking.notes: No product age, roadmap date, vendor claim, readiness number, prototype, weighted score, canary, deployment count, or online-traffic percentage is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem requires proof review; option filtering and scoring are bounded decision-structure examples.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled declared_ordinal_arithmetic_only.
Fixture limitations disclaim criteria completeness, valid scales/weights, feasibility, independence, uncertainty, maturity, evidence, transition, value, and authority.
Examples and exercises are synthetic teaching cases, not actual readiness assessments, refresh approvals, safety/security decisions, supplier qualifications, or operational authorizations.
Official sources are attributed without claiming NASA, GAO, DoD, or NIST review, approval, or endorsement of this chapter.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic arithmetic, source-backed guidance, internal review, independent readiness assessment, integrated V&V, and operational authority remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked capability framing, current baseline, roadmap alignment, refresh boundaries, critical technologies, contextual readiness, maturation versus integration, prototypes, alternatives, lifecycle value, change impact, evidence, transition, recovery, retirement, portfolio governance, and outcome measures.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked hardware/software/data/cloud refreshes, architecture seams, suppliers/tools, readiness evidence, staged gates, migration/coexistence, configuration/provenance, operations/training, fleet effectivity, adapters, recovery, contracts/rights, old-stack disposition, and portfolio capacity.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from capability gap and roadmap through maturity, alternatives, prototyping, impact, evidence, transition, operation, and retirement. Ten examples and five complete solutions cover compute, architecture, databases, heritage sensors, cloud, adapters, prototype limits, portfolios, old-stack closure, and scoring sensitivity.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/GAO/DoD/NIST expert, technology/readiness assessor, systems/domain engineer, architect, supplier/manufacturer, software/data/platform owner, human-factors specialist, operator/maintainer, safety/security/privacy authority, V&V/certification authority, finance/contracts/records authority, auditor, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
